test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 2 Feb 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: If the length of a rectangle is increased by 70%, what would be the percentage of decrease (correct to nearest integer) in the width to maintain the same area?
solution:
**Given:**

Increase in length of rectangle = 70%

**Concept Used:**

Area of rectangle = Length × Breadth

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the length of rectangle be x and breadth be y.

⇒ Area of rectangle = xy

⇒ New length after increase = x + 70% of x

⇒ New length after increase = x+(70)/(100)times x=x+(7x)/(10)=(17x)/(10)

⇒ As the area is same, the breadth will be,

⇒ Breadth = (xy)/(frac{17x){10}}=(10xy)/(17x)=(10y)/(17)

⇒ So, Percentage decrease in width = (7y)/(17)times (1)/(y)times 100=(700)/(17)=41.17\%

**Therefore, the percentage decrease in the width to maintain the same area is 41.17 %.**
